depiction.primary_object: two curved counter-clockwise arrows enclosed in a circle
depiction.composition: centered circular emblem with two opposing curved arrows inside

ambiguity: At small sizes, easily mistaken for the single counter-clockwise arrow inside a circle (undo, revert, or reset), especially since both can be loosely used for refresh or repeat.

modifier_semantics.meaning: frames the dual arrows as a standalone status badge or button

reasoning: Two curved arrows forming a circle inside a ring universally denote syncing, refreshing, or cycling/swapping. It fits tasks explicitly centered on data synchronization or periodic swaps, though it is visually interchangeable with many other sync/refresh/repeat icons and easily misused for generic 'update' verbs.

pass1.ambiguity: Nearly identical to other sync, refresh, repeat, or camera-flip icons that differ only in arrow direction or the outer circle.

distinguishing: Shows two opposing curved arrows chasing each other inside the circle (two-way sync, exchange, or continuous cycle), whereas the look-alike has only a single counter-clockwise arrow (undo, revert, or replay).
